newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein fetes Jordan's sporting heroes.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein fetes Jordan's sporting heroes.

text.p: Jordan welcomed home as conquering heroes on Monday its athletes from the pan-Arab games in Lebanon after they won more medals in a week than in four decades of previous competition.
King Hussein, who sent a military transport plane to pick up the athletes up from Beirut, greeted them one by one when they stepped off the aircraft to a red carpet reception.

Crown Prince Hassan, Queen Noor and a bevy of princes and cabinet ministers welcomed the competitors as bagpipes wailed and cheering supporters waved posters of Jordan's soccer team, who won the gold medal of the games on Sunday night.
The 1-0 victory over Syria triggered wild celebrations on the normally placid streets of the Jordanian capital.
Celebratory gunfire sounded across Amman, convoys of cars hooted their horns and youths in an affluent suburb of the city crowded into a public square singing late into the night.

The soccer gold, on top of two extra gold medals awarded to Jordan when two Egyptians were disqualified for drug-taking, lifted Jordan's tally to 10 gold medals, three more than its total haul in previous Arab Games since they began in 1953.
Its final ranking of fifth in the medal table was by far its strongest performance at the games and few cared that the kingdom was easily eclipsed by runaway winners Egypt, who won 97 gold medals.

Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali sent a message half way across the world from Malaysia to congratulate Jordan's soccer federation, whose win knocked the stumbling Middle East peace process off the front page of many newspapers.
"Jordan, Champion of the Arabs," said the banner headline of Ad-Dustour daily.
